method: Compared only this repair original-byte backups against the current changed service and tests, traced known-turn state ownership through admission, notifications, revision checks, closure and fresh-epoch recovery, and independently verified source and red/green evidence hashes. No test or product code was changed.
scope: src/runtime/service.ts changed guards plus surrounding activity/notification/newTurn/workflow/resume/close lifecycle
tests/runtime/service.test.ts added regressions and their FakeNative fixture, plus neighboring admission/recovery tests
tests/runtime/organization-native.test.ts complete test and exact backup diff
supportingReads: src/runtime/history.ts history admission and observe callback
src/runtime/workflows.ts mutation mode declarations and unsubscribe mode
reference/PROTOCOL-CONTRACT.md thread viewing/resume and completion contract
conclusions: Known turnId is counted independently of idle thread metadata in all changed status, admission, organization import, configuration and workflow guards. This closes the demonstrated second-turn admission gap without replacing the separate unknown/pending/goal/queue checks.

Matching turn/completed still sets status idle and turnId null. A completion for another turn leaves the known turn intact. Thread closed/deleted explicitly clears turn ownership. Interrupt remains available through its existing control path while work is active; resume keeps mode any.

Existing revision comparisons prevent an RPC response captured before a newer notification from re-applying old activity. An idle notification before matching completion no longer releases the turn. Completion before a later idle notification leaves turnId null. No additional permanent-busy path was found in these reviewed changes.

Unknown outcomes are intentionally retained after metadata or completion. Closing the old RuntimeService makes it unavailable; a fresh instance owns a new epoch and empty activity map, with complete-history admission still required. The added fixture demonstrates this recovery boundary rather than silently clearing unknown.

The native organization test subscribes to runtime events before conversation creation and waits for the exact thread/turn terminal notification with status completed. Existing idle status, metadata persistence, execution-root separation, history, one-provider-call and PID-death assertions are retained.

The definitive red records two second-turn promises resolving instead of rejecting; the final recorded targeted run has 62 passes including both idle cases, unknown/epoch recovery, and the native organization test. Source and raw hashes match organization.json.
limitations: This is a bounded review of one repair, not a complete repository audit or a new clean audit round. No full suite, targeted rerun, build, SSH, real model/MCP/account workflow or personal CODEX_HOME access was performed by this reviewer.

The reviewed lifecycle relies on the fixed contract terminal notifications and existing revision ordering. A lost completion intentionally leaves the current epoch conservative until recovery; this review does not claim a formal liveness proof or test every possible upstream event ordering.
The fresh-epoch regression uses a deterministic local fixture. The existing recorded native targeted test was inspected but not rerun independently.

The original uncaught list_turns full-run symptom was not independently reproduced by this reviewer, and organization.json explicitly retains that causal limitation. A full rerun remains parent-owned under the user-authorized exception.
